intro:
Chapter Two. The Path of Knowledge.
Arjuna has laid down his bow and asked for guidance. Now Krishna begins to teach. He speaks of the soul that is never born and never dies, of doing one's duty without clinging to its fruits, and of the person whose wisdom stands steady, like a flame in a windless place.

verses.1: Seeing Arjuna overcome with pity, his eyes brimming with tears, sinking in despair, Madhusudana spoke these words.
verses.2: Arjuna, where has this weakness come from, at a moment like this? It does not befit a noble soul. It leads neither to heaven, nor to honour.
verses.3: Do not give in to this unmanliness, Partha. It does not become you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart, and rise up, O scorcher of foes!
verses.4: Madhusudana, how can I fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle? They are worthy of my worship, O destroyer of enemies.
verses.5: Far better to live in this world on a beggar's alms than to kill these noble teachers. For if I kill them, every pleasure I enjoy here, every bit of wealth, will be stained with their blood.
verses.6: We do not even know which is better for us, that we conquer them, or that they conquer us. The very sons of Dhritarashtra, after killing whom we would not even wish to live, stand before us.
verses.7: My nature is overpowered by weakness and pity. My mind is confused about my duty. I am asking you, tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your disciple. I have taken refuge in you. Teach me.
verses.8: I see nothing that could drive away this grief that is drying up my senses. Not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth, nor lordship over the gods.
verses.9: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Arjuna, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, 'I will not fight', and fell silent.
verses.10: Then, O descendant of Bharata, there between the two armies, Hrishikesha, as if smiling, spoke these words to the grieving Arjuna.
verses.11: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living, nor for the dead.
verses.12: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings. Nor will there ever be a time when any of us shall cease to be.
verses.13: Just as the soul in this body passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so too it passes into another body. The steady one is not bewildered by this.
verses.14: Son of Kunti, when the senses touch their objects, they bring cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and they go. They do not last. Endure them, O Bharata.
verses.15: The one whom these cannot disturb, O best among men, who remains the same in pain and pleasure, steady and wise, that one is fit for immortality.
verses.16: The unreal has no being. The real never ceases to be. The seers of truth have seen the final truth of both.
verses.17: Know that That, which pervades all of this, is indestructible. No one can destroy the imperishable.
verses.18: These bodies of the eternal soul, which is indestructible and beyond measure, are said to come to an end. Therefore fight, O Bharata!
verses.19: One who thinks the soul is a killer, and one who thinks it is killed, both fail to understand. It does not kill, and it is not killed.
verses.20: It is never born, and it never dies. It did not come into being, and it will never cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.
verses.21: Partha, one who knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging, how can such a person kill anyone, or cause anyone to kill?
verses.22: Just as a person casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the soul casts off worn-out bodies, and enters into new ones.
verses.23: Weapons cannot cut it. Fire cannot burn it. Water cannot wet it. And the wind cannot dry it.
verses.24: It cannot be cut, or burnt, or wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, unmoving. It is everlasting.
verses.25: It is said to be unmanifest, unthinkable, and unchanging. So, knowing it to be this way, you should not grieve.
verses.26: And even if you think that it is constantly born and constantly dies, even then, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve.
verses.27: For death is certain for one who is born, and birth is certain for one who dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
verses.28: All beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their middle, and unmanifest again in their end, O Bharata. Why lament over this?
verses.29: Some see it as a wonder. Some speak of it as a wonder. Others hear of it as a wonder. And even after hearing of it, no one truly knows it.
verses.30: The one who dwells in the body of every being is eternal, and can never be killed, O Bharata. So you should not grieve for any creature.
verses.31: And considering your own duty, you should not waver. For a warrior, there is nothing higher than a righteous war.
verses.32: Fortunate are the warriors, Partha, who find such a war. It comes unsought, like an open gate to heaven!
verses.33: But if you will not fight this righteous war, then by abandoning your duty and your honour, you will bring sin upon yourself.
verses.34: People will speak of your disgrace forever. And for one who has been honoured, disgrace is worse than death.
verses.35: The great chariot warriors will think that you fled the battle out of fear. And those who held you in high esteem will think little of you.
verses.36: Your enemies will say many unspeakable things, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?
verses.37: If you are killed, you will attain heaven. If you win, you will enjoy the earth. So rise up, son of Kunti, determined to fight!
verses.38: Treat pleasure and pain alike, gain and loss, victory and defeat. Then engage in battle. In this way, you will incur no sin.
verses.39: So far I have told you the wisdom of Sankhya. Now hear the wisdom of Yoga. Joined with this wisdom, Partha, you will break free from the bondage of action.
verses.40: On this path, no effort is ever lost, and no harm is ever done. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verses.41: Here, O joy of the Kurus, the determined mind is one-pointed. But the thoughts of the undecided are endless, branching in many directions.
verses.42: The unwise delight in the flowery words of the Vedas, Partha. They say there is nothing else.
verses.43: Full of desires, with heaven as their highest goal, they speak of countless rituals that lead to rebirth, all aimed at pleasure and power.
verses.44: Those clinging to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such words, never find that determined mind which rests in samadhi.
verses.45: The Vedas deal with the three gunas. Rise above the three gunas, Arjuna. Be free of the pairs of opposites, ever steady in truth, free from worrying about gaining and keeping, and established in the Self.
verses.46: As much use as there is for a small well when there is water flooding everywhere, so much use are all the Vedas to one who truly knows.
verses.47: You have a right to your actions alone, never to their fruits. Do not let the fruits of action be your motive. And do not be attached to inaction either.
verses.48: Established in yoga, Dhananjaya, do your work, letting go of attachment, equal in success and in failure. This evenness of mind is called yoga.
verses.49: Action done for reward is far below action done with wisdom, Dhananjaya. Take refuge in that wisdom. Pitiable are those who work only for the fruits.
verses.50: One whose mind is joined with this wisdom lets go of both good and bad deeds, here in this very life. So devote yourself to yoga. Yoga is skill in action.
verses.51: The wise, joined with this wisdom, give up the fruits of action. Freed from the bonds of birth, they reach the state beyond all sorrow.
verses.52: When your mind crosses beyond the mire of delusion, you will no longer care for all that you have heard, or all that is yet to be heard.
verses.53: When your mind, now confused by conflicting teachings, stands unshaken and steady in samadhi, then you will attain yoga.
verses.54: Keshava, what are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady, who is established in samadhi? How does such a person speak? How do they sit? How do they walk?
verses.55: Partha, when a person lets go of every desire of the mind, and is content in the Self, by the Self alone, then that one is called steady in wisdom.
verses.56: One whose mind is not shaken in sorrow, who does not crave pleasures, who is free from attachment, fear and anger, that sage is called steady in wisdom.
verses.57: One who is without attachment anywhere, who neither rejoices when good things come, nor resents when bad things come, that person's wisdom is firmly set.
verses.58: When, like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, one fully withdraws the senses from their objects, that person's wisdom is firmly set.
verses.59: When a person stops feeding the senses, the objects fall away, but the taste for them remains. Even that taste falls away, once the Supreme is seen.
verses.60: Son of Kunti, the restless senses forcefully carry away the mind, even of a wise person who is striving for control.
verses.61: Restraining them all, one should sit steady, devoted to me. For one whose senses are under control, that person's wisdom is firmly set.
verses.62: When a person dwells on the objects of the senses, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire. And from desire comes anger.
verses.63: From anger comes delusion. From delusion, the loss of memory. From the loss of memory, the ruin of reason. And when reason is ruined, a person is lost.
verses.64: But a person of self-control, moving among the objects of the senses with senses free from attraction and aversion, and governed by the Self, attains serenity.
verses.65: In that serenity, all sorrows come to an end. For the mind of one who is serene soon becomes firmly steady.
verses.66: For one who is not united, there is no wisdom, and no meditation. Without meditation there is no peace. And without peace, how can there be happiness?
verses.67: When the mind runs after the wandering senses, it carries away one's wisdom, just as the wind carries away a boat on the water.
verses.68: Therefore, mighty-armed one, when a person's senses are completely withdrawn from their objects, that person's wisdom is firmly set.
verses.69: What is night for all beings, there the self-controlled one is awake. And where all beings are awake, that is night for the sage who truly sees.
verses.70: As rivers flow into the ocean, which is always full, yet never disturbed, so the one into whom all desires flow finds peace. Not the one who chases after desires.
verses.71: One who gives up all desires, and moves through life free from longing, without any sense of 'mine', and without ego, that one attains peace.
verses.72: This, Partha, is the state of Brahman. Having reached it, one is never deluded again. Established in it, even at the hour of death, one attains the bliss of Brahman.

notes.7: This is the turning point of the Gita. Arjuna stops arguing and says, 'I am your disciple. Teach me.' Real learning begins the moment we admit that we do not know.
notes.20: Krishna's first teaching is about who we really are. The body is born and dies, but the Self within it was never born and can never be destroyed. Everything else in the Gita rests on this.
notes.47: Perhaps the most famous verse of the Gita. Do your work fully and sincerely, but do not let the reward be the reason. When we stop clinging to results, we are free from anxiety and can give our best.
notes.63: Verses sixty-two and sixty-three trace a chain: thinking about something leads to attachment, then desire, anger, confusion, forgetting, and finally ruin. Catching the first link, where the mind lingers, is the key.
notes.70: The ocean receives every river and yet stays within its shores. A steady person, too, can let desires come and go without being moved by them. That is where peace is found.
